introduction.text: Chiesa di Sant'Agnese in Agone is a 17th‑century Baroque church in Rome that serves as a titular deaconry and a cultural venue, notable for its architectural rivalry between Borromini and Bernini and its richly decorated interior.

history.description: Construction of the church began in 1652 under the patronage of Pope Innocent X, with architects Girolamo and Carlo Rainaldi.
In 1653 the Rainaldis were replaced by Francesco Borromini, who introduced a concave façade and a central dome.
By 1655 Pope Innocent X had died; the façade had reached the top of the lower order, but the project stalled.
In 1657 Borromini resigned after losing support, and Carlo Rainaldi was reappointed.
The pendentives of the dome were painted with the Cardinal Virtues between 1662 and 1672 by Giovanni Battista Gaulli.
In 1668 Camillo Borghese took over responsibility for the church, reinstating Carlo Rainaldi and commissioning Ciro Ferri for dome frescoes.
The cupola fresco of the Apotheosis of Saint Agnes was begun in 1670 by Ciro Ferri and finished in 1689 by Sebastiano Corbellini.
The Two Holy Families relief was completed in 1676 by Domenico Guidi.
The church has served as a titular deaconry, with Gerhard Ludwig Müller as the current Cardinal‑Deacon since 2014.

design.description: The façade features a concave profile with twin towers framing a central dome, a design influenced by Bernini's bell towers at Saint Peter's.
Curved steps descend from the façade to Piazza Navona, creating an oval landing that harmonises the building with the piazza.
The interior follows a Greek cross plan, with a near‑circular nave and marble sculptural masterpieces dedicated to martyred saints.

art.description: Cupola fresco of the Apotheosis of Saint Agnes (1670–1689) by Ciro Ferri and Sebastiano Corbellini.
Pendentives painted with the Cardinal Virtues (1662–1672) by Giovanni Battista Gaulli.
Sacristy painting Glory of Saint Agnes by Paolo Gismondi.
The Two Holy Families relief (1676) by Domenico Guidi.
Sculptural reliefs of the Martyrdom of Saint Eustace by Melchiorre Cafà and collaborators.
Statues of Saint Agnes and Saint Sebastian in illusionistic marble architecture by Pier Paolo Campi and Pierre Le Gros.
